title: Jean Vigne, his hall, and bass drummer Giles
summary: Vigne's daughter and the coal yard rehearsals in Storyville; Giles's funeral was the last one his father played.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I don't know. The lady was over there, the sort of superintendent of the hall. Of the building. That's Jean Vigne's daughter. Oh, I didn't know.
Yeah, that's his daughter. The Jeannemie Hall. The Jeannemie Hall, yeah.
At the time you made the record, then we got to see her. Yes.
But let us in the back door or something. Yeah, she's still there, right? No.
The one that prepared the sandwiches and things.
Oh, yeah? Yeah, well, that's his daughter. That's Jean Vigne's daughter. She probably know a good deal about it.
Oh, yeah, I'm sure she can. Get plenty of it.

Yeah, I can remember him. I was just where the Iberville Project is now, which was part of Storyville at the time. Well, he used to run a wooden cold yard, and he, and I know my daddy, and then they would have rehearsals sometime in the back of the cold yard some days when business would be slow and the guys would meet around there. And I can remember him from that area, going there, listening to them rehearsal. I was just about seven, six years old around the time I can recall. Very interesting. Yeah, Jean Vigne, Mike Murray, D.D. Chandler, and my father, all of it was around the same period, and I guess just about on the same type. Uh-huh. Because those were the ones that I often heard it mention about. Also, this other fellow, well he strictly played just bass drum and a brass band was Giles. Now what's Giles' first name? I can't remember.
Yeah, I can't remember now. Wait a minute.

I don't know. But was the uncle's name? I don't know. I don't know if it was relative or not. But I know his name was Giles. That was the last funeral that my father played, because Giles' funeral was just about a month or a month and a half before my father.
